Subject: Hosted API pricing request — Elara Health (initial ask)

Ben / Marissa —

Quick background: Elara Health (Samantha Lee, procurement copied) is asking for a one-time concession on Hosted API list pricing. They are proposing a 12-month committed usage with a 2-region deployment (US + EU) and will sign a 12-month SOW with a start date of 2027-01-15. Their ask: 27% off list for Hosted API usage.

Why this matters:
- ARR impact: forecasted $1.1M ARR in year 1 on committed usage; potential $3.2M over 3 years with expected adoption of additional routes.
- Strategic: Elara has a technology partnership program and has offered a marketplace spotlight + case study if we approve commercial terms.
- Risk/controls: they require SOC2 evidence (we can provide), standard data residency (US/EU), and an SOC-2 addendum in SOW (legal OK in principle).

Ask: I need guidance on escalation to exec for >20% discount authorization. Attached: Elara_SOW_v2.pdf (redlines) and usage_forecast_Q4-2026.xlsx.

Proposed guardrails if approved: 12-month commitment, non-refundable onboarding credit of $50k, quarterly usage reviews, automatic reversion to standard list in year 2 unless recommitted.

Appreciate quick thoughts — timeline is tight; procurement wants a commercial response by next Tuesday (2026-11-23).

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

Thanks for the overview. A few rapid notes:

- Need clarity on net new revenue vs. migration of existing hosted spend (we should avoid subsidizing existing contracts). The attachment looks like a mix of new and migrated traffic; can you separate?
- Precedent: who else has received similar concessions? We must document precedent to avoid blanket approval.

Can you provide:
1) A 1‑page executive summary with exact ARR uplift and margin impact (post-discount).
2) Confirmation that Marketplace + case study is on the table and any timelines.
3) Signed LOI or email from procurement indicating intent to commit (even if conditional).

I can prepare the deal desk memo once we have the numbers and a clear list of conditional concessions (SLA, onshore support, credits).

-Ben
